chief_complaint: Chronic disease management focusing on hypertension, early diabetic kidney disease, hyperlipidemia, and obesity
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 61-year-old white male with a long-standing history of obesity (since 1989) and hyperlipidemia (diagnosed 2011). Essential hypertension was identified in 2018 and is currently treated with low‑dose lisinopril and amlodipine, yielding a normal blood pressure reading (104/64 mmHg) but a low diastolic that may reflect over‑treatment. In mid‑2021, both chronic kidney disease stage 1 and a disorder of the kidney due to diabetes mellitus were documented, indicating early diabetic nephropathy despite the absence of recorded antidiabetic therapy or recent A1c values. Osteoarthritis of the hip, diagnosed in 2009, is managed with chronic naproxen sodium, which poses additional risk to renal function. The patient remains employed full‑time but has only a primary‑school education, suggesting potential health‑literacy challenges. Recent preventive visits have been regular, but laboratory data (eGFR, lipid panel, A1c, BMI) are missing, limiting objective assessment of disease control.
